page: Vultr voc-g-8c-32gb-160s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, configured with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a 160 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and memory bandwidth metrics fall within the average range. The instance achieves a static web serving throughput of 8.45 GB/sec and handles 15.29 million Redis SET operations per second.

While the instance performs adequately on smaller workloads, it exhibits performance limitations on larger computational tasks. For example, LLM inference prompt processing with a medium 7B model is weak, scoring in the bottom 25%, though text generation for the same model remains average. Consequently, this server is best suited for general-purpose workloads, mid-tier database operations, static web serving, and lightweight serialization or compression tasks rather than heavy LLM or parallelized high-performance computing.
description: The Vultr voc-g-8c-32gb-160s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 8 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs, 32.0 GB of RAM, and 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, this server delivers strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of stress-ng benchmarks. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations remain in the average tier. A key tradeoff is its weak performance in processing prompts for medium-sized LLM models, though it maintains average speeds for text generation. This hardware profile makes the instance highly suitable for general-purpose applications, static web serving, and moderate database workloads where dedicated CPU resources and fast local storage are required.
